62382-thralls-of-the-endless-night.title: Thralls Of The Endless Night
62382-thralls-of-the-endless-night.creator: Unknown
62382-thralls-of-the-endless-night.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. eft to the little curve of the horizon. Rocks on it, and edible moss. Wind-made gullies with grey shrubs thick in their bottoms, guarding their sour white berries with thorns and sacs of poisoned dust that burst when touched.

arxiv-2406-02372.title: Braided scalar quantum field theory
arxiv-2406-02372.description: Abstract We formulate scalar field theories in a curved braided L ∞ L_{\infty} -algebra formalism and analyse their correlation functions using Batalin–Vilkovisky quantization. We perform detailed calculations in cubic braided scalar field theory up to two-loop order and three-point multiplicity.

arxiv-2410-15733.title: Non-thermal production of Higgsino dark matter by late-decaying scalar fields
arxiv-2410-15733.creator: Hajime Fukuda, Qiang Li, Takeo Moroi, Atsuya Niki
arxiv-2410-15733.description: Abstract We study the non-thermal production of the Higgsino dark matter (DM). Assuming that the lightest neutral Higgsino is the lightest supersymmetric particle (LSP) in the minimal supersymmetric standard model, we calculate the relic abundance of the Higgsino LSP produced by the decay of late-decaying scalar field.

arxiv-2411-09535.title: Adaptive dynamics of direct reciprocity with N N rounds of memory
arxiv-2411-09535.creator: N. Balabanova, H. Duong, C. Hilbe
arxiv-2411-09535.description: Abstract Abstract: The theory of direct reciprocity explores how individuals cooperate when they interact repeatedly. In repeated interactions, individuals can condition their behaviour on what happened earlier. One prominent example of a conditional strategy is Tit-for-Tat, which prescribes to cooperate if and only if the co-player did so in the previous round.

arxiv-2507-02888.title: Acceleration of the CASINO quantum Monte Carlo software using graphics processing units and OpenACC Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-2507-02888.creator: B. Thorpe, M. J. Smith, P. J. Hasnip, N. D. Drummond
arxiv-2507-02888.description: Abstract We describe how quantum Monte Carlo calculations using the CASINO software can be accelerated using graphics processing units (GPUs) and OpenACC. In particular we consider offloading Ewald summation, the evaluation of long-range two-body terms in the Jastrow correlation factor, and the evaluation of orbitals in a blip basis set.

arxiv-2512-24868.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guglielmo Coloretti ID, Andreas Crivellin ID, Howard E. Haber ID. pmc-10591038.title: Prostate cancer immunotherapy: Improving clinical outcomes with a multi-pronged approach
pmc-10591038.creator: Dhivya Sridaran, Elliot Bradshaw, Carl DeSelm, Russell Pachynski, Kiran Mahajan, Nupam P. Mahajan
pmc-10591038.description: SummaryCancer immunotherapy has gained traction in recent years owing to remarkable tumor clearance in some patients. Despite the notable success of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in multiple malignancies, engagement of the immune system for targeted prostate cancer (PCa) therapy is still in its infancy.

pmc-10724595.title: Association of dietary patterns of pregnant women with pregnancy outcomes: A hospital‐based study
pmc-10724595.creator: Sahar Ghorbani‐Kafteroodi, Maryam Ghiasvand, Maryam Saghafi‐Asl, Soudabeh Kazemi Aski
pmc-10724595.description: Diet is one of the main factors influencing pregnancy outcomes. Maternal and child health both seem to be related to dietary patterns. So far, no study on dietary pattern has been performed on pregnant women and its association with pregnancy outcomes in Rasht. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the association between dietary patterns and pregnancy outcomes in Rasht.

pmc-10738550.title: LIFE COURSE TIMING OF ADVERSITY AND DIURNAL CORTISOL IN LATER LIFE
pmc-10738550.creator: Nadine Sikora, Briana Mezuk, James Abelson, Jane Rafferty, Jamie Abelson, Julie Ober Allen
pmc-10738550.description: Exposure to adversity is believed to alter stress sensitive biological processes. One manifestation of this, flatter diurnal cortisol slopes, has been linked to cardiometabolic problems. Questions remain about whether the timing of adversity within the life course influences its effect on cortisol slopes in later life.

pmc-11305560.title: The use of mare’s milk for yogurt ice cream and synbiotic ice cream production
pmc-11305560.creator: Katarzyna Szkolnicka, Anna Mituniewicz-Małek, Izabela Dmytrów, Elżbieta Bogusławska-Wąs
pmc-11305560.description: During the last years, growing interest in the use of mare’s milk in food production is observed. The subject of the study was to evaluate the feasibility of mare’s milk for the production of yogurt ice cream and synbiotic ice cream.

pmc-11572739.title: N‐acetylcysteine as a treatment for substance use cravings: A meta‐analysis
pmc-11572739.creator: Emma L Winterlind, Samantha G Malone, Michael R Setzer, Mikela A Murphy, David Saunders, Joshua C Gray
pmc-11572739.description: N‐acetylcysteine (NAC) may serve as a novel pharmacotherapy for substance use and substance craving in individuals with substance use disorders (SUDs), possibly through its potential to regulate glutamate. Though prior meta‐analyses generally support NAC's efficacy in reducing symptoms of craving, individual trials have found mixed results.

pmc-11641549.title: Silencing of the MP Gene via dsRNA Affects Root Development and Growth in the Invasive Weed Mikania micrantha
pmc-11641549.creator: Zhenghui Ou, Yuantong Zhang, Qiang Wu, Kangkang Wang, Guangzhong Zhang, Xi Qiao, Ying Yan, Wanqiang Qian, Fanghao Wan, Bo Liu
pmc-11641549.description: Mikania micrantha (“mile-a-minute” weed) is a global invasive alien weed that can cause severe damage to agroforestry ecosystems and significant agricultural losses worldwide. Although chemical, manual, or mechanical control methods are widely used to control M. micrantha, RNA interference (RNAi)-based biocontrol methods have rarely been reported for this species.

pmc-11655742.title: Rapid, multiplex and automated detection of bacteria and fungi in endophthalmitis via a microfluidic real-time pcr system
pmc-11655742.creator: Siyu Wang, Yiteng Liu, Yingqi Li, Yibo Gao, Zhongliang Zou, Na Xu, Qi Song, Fangyan Liu, Yihong Song, Xian Wang, Zixin Fan
pmc-11655742.description: BackgroundEndophthalmitis is an ophthalmologic emergency requiring accurate and rapid diagnosis for treatment. Currently, the diagnosis commonly relies on culture and molecular biology, which falls short of clinical rapid diagnosis. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a self-build Microfluidic Real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) System for rapidly identifying potential pathogens of endophthalmitis.

pmc-12428563.title: Preliminary Development of a Health Education Program to Improve Psychological Distress Among Patients with Esophageal Cancer and Their Partners: A Narrative Review
pmc-12428563.creator: Meng Wei, Caryn Mei Hsien Chan, Azlina Yusuf, Maziah Ahmad Marzuki, Paolo Cotogni
pmc-12428563.description: Background: The diagnosis and treatment of esophageal cancer often leads to complex and long-lasting psychological distress, such as anxiety and depression, in patients and their partners. This psychological distress can not only potentially worsen the poor prognosis of the disease, but also reduce health-related quality of life by affecting the patient’s ability to function and enjoy life.

pmc-12547259.title: Biopolymer-based active packaging with TiO₂ and nano-encapsulated essential oils improves postharvest stability of fresh-cut kale
pmc-12547259.creator: Faezeh Mirzajani, Raheleh Ebrahimi, Weria Weisany, Orang Khademi
pmc-12547259.description: Fresh-cut kale (Brassica oleracea) is highly perishable due to dehydration, enzymatic browning, membrane damage, and microbial spoilage. This study developed an active packaging system using chitosan-based nanocomposite films containing titanium dioxide (TiO₂) nanoparticles and nanoencapsulated essential oils (EO-NCs) from Thymus daenensis Celak and Bunium persicum.

pmc-12613185.title: Prevalence of Fusarium sp. in juvenile olive ridley sea turtles (Lepidochelys olivacea) kept at the Centro de Conservación Marina, Taxisco, Santa Rosa, Guatemala
pmc-12613185.creator: Luis S. Figueroa, Jacqueline Escobar, Martín Yllescas
pmc-12613185.description: Background:The olive ridley sea turtle (Lepidochelys olivacea) is experiencing population declines due to both anthropogenic impacts and emerging biological threats, including fungal pathogens such as Fusarium spp.Aim:This study aimed to determine the prevalence of Fusarium spp. in juvenile L. olivacea individuals housed at the Centro de Conservación Marina (CCM) in Guatemala.

pmc-12716725.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4 in the development of family medicine residency examinations
pmc-12716725.creator: Hanu Chaudhari, Christopher Meaney, Kulamakan Kulasegaram, Fok-Han Leung
pmc-12716725.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Creating high-quality medical examinations is challenging due to time, cost, and training requirements. This study evaluates the use of ChatGPT 4.0 (ChatGPT-4) in generating medical exam questions for postgraduate family medicine (FM) trainees. Develop a standardized method for postgraduate multiple-choice medical exam question creation using ChatGPT-4 and compare the effectiveness of large language model (LLM) generated questions to those created by human experts.

pmc-12825964.title: Discovery of a novel whitefly- and aphid-transmitted polerovirus on rice plants with dwarfing and fewer tillering symptoms
pmc-12825964.creator: Jiaping Yu, Ming Zeng, Yali Zhou, Jirui Wang, Xueping Zhou, Jianxiang Wu
pmc-12825964.description: Rice is the most important cereal grain worldwide and is cultivated mainly in Asian countries. Rice viral disease epidemics caused by insect-borne viruses are a major threat to rice production. However, to date, how many unknown viruses naturally infect rice plants in the field remains vague.

pmc-13015171.title: The diagnostic performance of point-of-care tests for serum amyloid A and C-reactive protein in lame sows
pmc-13015171.creator: Nadia Jakobsen, Inge Larsen, Nicolai Rosager Weber, Ken Steen Pedersen
pmc-13015171.description: BackgroundFor acute phase proteins to be implemented in routine diagnostics for pig herds, a fast, reliable, and portable point-of-care test is required. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of two point-of-care tests on lame gestating sows. The two tests were the Cobas b101 CRP test for C-reactive protein and OmniChekTM-SAA for serum amyloid A.

pmc-13543575.title: A third-generation, high-affinity biparatopic anti-tau antibody inhibits intracellular tau aggregation seeded by Alzheimer’s brain extracts
pmc-13543575.creator: Eric Hatterer, Lucile Broyer, Sara Pecoraro, Fabien Cusin, Naz Simsek, John J Breve, Mathieu Clavel, Kevin L. Batenburg, Bart Klein, Thuur Zuidweg, Kristin Piché, Jeremie Bourguignon, Margot Bonnet-Gamard, Pauline Malinge, Franck Gueneau, Valery Moine, Nadia Anceriz, Krzysztof Masternak, Nicolas Fis
pmc-13543575.description: BackgroundTau immunotherapy has recently shown clinical promise but required high dosing. We developed NIDB-3101, a novel third-generation, high-affinity anti-tau biparatopic antibody designed for superior tau binding, aggregation inhibition, and extended half-life.MethodsNIDB-3101 binds tau’s microtubule-binding region and C-terminal domains. Various binding and cellular functional assays using recombinants, but more importantly human AD extracts were used to assess NIDB-3101 benefits.

pmc-13546684.title: Patient‑Reported Outcome Measures for Food Preference in Adults: A COSMIN‑Based Systematic Review
pmc-13546684.creator: Yun-Xia Wang, Ting Liu, Zhi-Shui Wu, Yin-Ying Zhang, Jian-Zheng Cai
pmc-13546684.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundFood preference is a key determinant of eating behavior and dietary choice in adults. Reliable and valid assessment tools are essential for tailoring dietary interventions, increasing adherence, and improving clinical and nutritional outcomes.ObjectiveTo systematically identify and evaluate the psychometric properties of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) assessing food preference in adults, specifically focusing on the evidence provided in their initial development and validation reports.DesignSystematic review of measurement properties conducted in accordance with the COSMIN guidelines.MethodsWe searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL
